claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're caring for.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you currently have any children under your care that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

Please let me know their names and ages, if you do.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now I need to gather some details about your circumstances. Let me start with this:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and maintenance?** In other words, do you live with Alex and provide for their everyday needs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me and I look after them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's helpful to know.

**What is your current residency status in the UK?** For example, are you a British citizen, an EU citizen, or do you have another immigration status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't currently live in the UK. I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's important information.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have British nationality?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd prefer not to get into all those details right now - I just want to know if I can claim Child Benefit for Alex. Does living abroad affect my eligibility?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand, and I appreciate you asking directly. Yes, your residency status does affect Child Benefit eligibility, so I do need to gather a bit more information to give you an accurate answer.

Let me ask this more simply:

**Do you have a right to reside in the UK?** This includes being a British citizen, having settled status, or having another qualifying immigration status that allows you to live in the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have a right to reside in the UK - I'm living abroad with Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me, you are currently living abroad and do not have a right to reside in the UK. Child Benefit eligibility requires that you have a right to reside in the UK. Since you don't meet this requirement, I'm afraid you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

However, if your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you return to the UK and establish a right to reside—you may become eligible then.

conversation.text: Is there anything else I can help you with?
